```{r setup, message = FALSE}
# ---- Setup ----
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

theme_set(theme_minimal())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.5)
```

This document introduces the Global Power Plant Database, prepares it for analysis, and explores how
the world's generating capacity is split by fuel, how that has changed over time, and where it sits.
The same steps are implemented in Python in `python/01_data_preparation_eda.ipynb`.

# 1. The dataset

The **Global Power Plant Database** (version 1.3.0; Global Energy Observatory, Google, KTH Royal
Institute of Technology, Enipedia and World Resources Institute, 2021; CC BY 4.0) lists 34,936 power
plants in 167 countries, with each plant's capacity (MW), location, primary fuel, commissioning year
(when known), reported generation for 2013–2019 where available, and WRI's modelled (estimated)
generation for 2013–2017. It is a 2021 snapshot.

```{r load}
raw <- read.csv("../data/global_power_plant_database.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                na.strings = "")
dim(raw)
cat("Countries:", n_distinct(raw$country_long), "\n")

raw %>%
  group_by(primary_fuel) %>%
  summarise(plants = n(), capacity_GW = round(sum(capacity_mw) / 1000, 1)) %>%
  mutate(share_of_capacity_pct = round(capacity_GW / sum(capacity_GW) * 100, 1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(plants))
```

# 2. Data quality

```{r missing}
missing <- data.frame(column = names(raw), pct_missing = round(colMeans(is.na(raw)) * 100, 1)) %>%
  filter(pct_missing > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_missing))
missing

# Is the commissioning year missing equally often for every fuel?
raw %>%
  group_by(primary_fuel) %>%
  summarise(pct_year_missing = round(mean(is.na(commissioning_year)) * 100, 1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_year_missing))
```

**Interpretation.** Capacity, location and primary fuel are complete. The commissioning year is missing
for `r round(mean(is.na(raw$commissioning_year)) * 100, 1)`% of plants, and unevenly: about two thirds
of solar plants lack it, against about a fifth of coal plants. WRI's estimated generation for 2017 is
available for `r round(mean(!is.na(raw$estimated_generation_gwh_2017)) * 100, 1)`% of plants.

# 3. Preparation

```{r prepare}
df <- raw

# (1) Fuel groups: the six largest fuels keep their label; the nine small ones become 'Other'
main_fuels <- c("Solar", "Hydro", "Wind", "Gas", "Coal", "Oil")
df$fuel <- ifelse(df$primary_fuel %in% main_fuels, df$primary_fuel, "Other")

# (2) Broad category used in the trend analysis
category_map <- c(Solar = "Renewable", Wind = "Renewable", Hydro = "Renewable",
                  Biomass = "Renewable", Geothermal = "Renewable", "Wave and Tidal" = "Renewable",
                  Coal = "Fossil", Gas = "Fossil", Oil = "Fossil", Petcoke = "Fossil",
                  Cogeneration = "Fossil", Nuclear = "Nuclear")
df$category <- unname(category_map[df$primary_fuel])
df$category[is.na(df$category)] <- "Other"

# (3) Capacity spans 1 to 22,500 MW, so a log10 version is used for modelling
df$log_capacity <- log10(df$capacity_mw)

# (4) Missing commissioning years: filled with the overall median year, plus a missing flag
df$year_missing <- as.integer(is.na(df$commissioning_year))
median_year <- median(df$commissioning_year, na.rm = TRUE)
df$comm_year <- ifelse(is.na(df$commissioning_year), median_year, df$commissioning_year)
cat("Median commissioning year used for filling:", median_year, "\n")

# (5) Whether the plant lists any secondary fuel
df$multi_fuel <- as.integer(!is.na(df$other_fuel1))

# (6) Estimated capacity factor (for the leakage check in Part 2 only)
df$capacity_factor_est <- pmin(df$estimated_generation_gwh_2017 / (df$capacity_mw * 8.76), 1)

df <- df %>% select(country, country_long, name, capacity_mw, log_capacity, latitude, longitude,
                    primary_fuel, fuel, category, commissioning_year, comm_year, year_missing,
                    multi_fuel, capacity_factor_est)
dim(df)
sort(table(df$fuel), decreasing = TRUE)
```

# 4. Exploratory analysis

## 4.1 Plants and capacity by fuel

```{r eda-fuel}
by_fuel <- df %>%
  group_by(fuel) %>%
  summarise(plants = n(), capacity_GW = round(sum(capacity_mw) / 1000, 1),
            median_MW = median(capacity_mw)) %>%
  arrange(desc(capacity_GW))

ggplot(by_fuel, aes(reorder(fuel, -plants), plants)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Number of Plants by Fuel", x = "Primary fuel group", y = "Number of plants")

ggplot(by_fuel, aes(reorder(fuel, -capacity_GW), capacity_GW)) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkorange") +
  labs(title = "Total Capacity by Fuel", x = "Primary fuel group", y = "Capacity (GW)")

by_fuel
```

**Interpretation.** Solar has the most plants
(`r format(by_fuel$plants[by_fuel$fuel == "Solar"], big.mark = ",")`) but only
`r by_fuel$capacity_GW[by_fuel$fuel == "Solar"]` GW, because its median plant is
`r by_fuel$median_MW[by_fuel$fuel == "Solar"]` MW. Coal has
`r format(by_fuel$plants[by_fuel$fuel == "Coal"], big.mark = ",")` plants but the most capacity
(`r format(by_fuel$capacity_GW[by_fuel$fuel == "Coal"], big.mark = ",")` GW), with a median plant of
`r by_fuel$median_MW[by_fuel$fuel == "Coal"]` MW.

## 4.2 Plant size by fuel

```{r eda-size}
ggplot(df, aes(reorder(fuel, -capacity_mw, median), capacity_mw)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue", outlier.size = 0.3) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(title = "Plant Capacity by Fuel (log scale)", x = "Primary fuel group",
       y = "Capacity (MW, log scale)")
```

**Interpretation.** Typical coal and gas plants are hundreds of MW, while solar and wind plants are
mostly a few MW to tens of MW, so size will help separate fuels in Question 1.

## 4.3 How the mix of new capacity has changed

```{r eda-trend}
trend <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(commissioning_year), commissioning_year >= 1950) %>%
  mutate(decade = floor(commissioning_year / 10) * 10) %>%
  group_by(decade, category) %>%
  summarise(GW = sum(capacity_mw) / 1000, .groups = "drop")

ggplot(trend, aes(factor(decade), GW, fill = category)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Fossil = "dimgray", Nuclear = "gold", Renewable = "seagreen",
                               Other = "lightsteelblue")) +
  labs(title = "Capacity Added per Decade by Category (plants with a known year)",
       x = "Decade commissioned", y = "Capacity added (GW)", fill = "Category")

shares <- trend %>%
  group_by(decade) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(GW / sum(GW) * 100, 1)) %>%
  select(-GW) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = category, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0)
shares
```

**Interpretation.** Fossil fuels made up most new capacity in every decade from the 1950s to the 2010s,
peaking at `r shares$Fossil[shares$decade == 2000]`% in the 2000s. Renewables' share of new capacity
rose to `r shares$Renewable[shares$decade == 2010]`% in the 2010s and to
`r shares$Renewable[shares$decade == 2020]`% for plants commissioned in 2020, the last year in the
snapshot. Missing years (most often for solar and wind) mean these figures understate recent renewable
additions.

## 4.4 The largest countries

```{r eda-countries, fig.height = 5.5}
top <- df %>%
  group_by(country_long) %>%
  mutate(total = sum(capacity_mw)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(dense_rank(desc(total)) <= 12) %>%
  group_by(country_long, fuel) %>%
  summarise(GW = sum(capacity_mw) / 1000, .groups = "drop")

ggplot(top, aes(reorder(country_long, GW, sum), GW, fill = fuel)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Capacity Mix of the 12 Largest Countries", x = "Country", y = "Capacity (GW)",
       fill = "Fuel")
```

```{r save}
dir.create("../data/processed", showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(df, "../data/processed/power_plants_clean_r.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("Saved", dim(df), "\n")
```

# 5. Summary

The prepared data cover 34,936 plants with complete capacity, location and fuel; commissioning year is
known for half. Solar dominates by plant count, coal by capacity, and renewables' share of new capacity
has risen sharply since the 2000s. Question 1 predicts each plant's fuel group; Question 2 clusters
countries by their capacity mix.
